messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
**Dark mode is here**

We shipped dark mode today. It's in 3.2, on iOS, Android, and the web app.

This took longer than it should have, and the reason is worth saying out loud: the first version we built was just an inverted stylesheet. Pure black background, pure white text. It looked fine in a screenshot and was miserable to read for more than ten minutes — the contrast ratio was so high that text seemed to vibrate against the background. So we threw it out and started over with a designer who has spent years on typography for screens.

What you get instead is a near-black background (#16161A) with off-white text at about 87% opacity. Your highlights, code blocks, and inline links all got their own palettes rather than inheriting a global inversion, which is why a yellow highlight still reads as yellow instead of glowing like a hazard sign. Images and embedded PDFs stay untouched. We tested this on OLED phones at 2am, which is when most of you are writing anyway, based on our usage graphs.

Turn it on in Settings → Appearance. Three options: Light, Dark, and Match System. Match System follows your OS schedule, so it flips at sunset if that's how your phone is configured.

One caveat. Custom themes made before 3.2 won't have dark variants and will fall back to light. We're working on a migration path and expect it in 3.3, sometime next month.

Tell us what breaks. The feedback thread is pinned in the community forum.
